---
title: "ENTICES worked examples"
output: html_document
---

These examples are what a production regeneration needs: how to set up the circulation model,
generate an input, run PHREEQC, read the output, pair a run with its blank, and run the two
options (the cometary-ice ocean and the pore-gas bracket). Run from the repo root, after the
self-tests pass (README §3). Each chunk is `eval = FALSE`: they take minutes to tens of minutes.
Numbers quoted are from PHREEQC 3.8.6 on 2026-10-28; Lucas's earlier notebook is
`examples/ENTICES_runs_lucas_2026-10.Rmd`.

```{r setup, eval = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
source("ENTICES_LF_20260917.R")   # also sources iom_module.R, phreeqc_tools.R, organic_contribution.R
```

## The circulation model and the PHREEQC parameters

`Simulator` computes the tidal flow through the porous core; `PhreeqcIntegrator` turns it into
masses normalised to the permeable layer (rock 1 kg, porewater ~0.08–0.16 kg, ocean 0.34 kg).
`k` (m²) and `layer_thickness` (m) are the circulation parameters; 194.2 km is the whole core.

```{r model}
sim <- Simulator$new(k = 1e-7, layer_thickness = 194200, config = EnceladusConfig$new())
sim$run_simulation()
ph <- PhreeqcIntegrator$new(sim)
ph$calculate_phreeqc_parameters(organic_wt_percent = 15)   # 15 wt% IOM in the rock
ph$profile_file                                            # profiles/...: 261.2 atm porewater, 66.7 atm ocean
run_input <- function(f) {                                 # run a .pqi with the database in its header
  db <- sub("^# Database: ", "", grep("^# Database: ", readLines(f, n = 20), value = TRUE))
  r <- run_phreeqc(f, db, output = sub("\\.pqi$", ".out", f), workdir = dirname(f))
  stopifnot(r$errors == 0)
  x <- read.delim(sub("\\.pqi$", ".csv", f), check.names = FALSE, strip.white = TRUE)
  names(x) <- trimws(names(x)); x[trimws(x$state) == "react", ]
}
```

## 1. A 25 °C smoke test (minutes)

Two orbits of `tidal_kinetic` at 25 °C. The C seed (`trace_C_molal = 1e-14`) is needed at 25 °C:
the IOM releases almost no carbon, and PHREEQC can't solve a carbon balance with none.

```{r smoke}
f <- ph$generate_phreeqc_input_tidal_kinetic(output_dir = "phreeqc_inputs/ex1", mode = "ungrouped",
                                             n_orbital_cycles = 2, porewater_temp = 25, trace_C_molal = 1e-14)
x <- run_input(f)
x[c(5, 8), c("soln", "pH", "Na", "mu", "m_H2", "C", "Vgas_L", "Vgas_Vpore")]   # orbit 2: porewater (REACT), ocean (MIX 2)
```

Expect (20 s; numbers of 2026-10-31: skin box, φc 0.4, ΔP from the strain, exchange 6e-6 per
half-orbit): at orbit 2 a porewater of pH 11.04, 0.115 molal Na, ionic strength 0.26; an ocean of pH
7.57 with 0.065 molal H₂ (saturated at 66.7 atm) and DIC 9.6e-15 (the seed: the IOM releases almost none
at 25 °C); 0.90 L of ocean gas. The metal's H₂ forms a pore bubble of 0.44 L, 2.8× the pore volume, in
the first orbit; under the default `pore_gas_fate = "to_ocean"` it goes to the ocean, which it
saturates. `pore_gas_fate = "retain_to_pore_volume"` keeps the bubble up to the pore volume and still
saturates the ocean (pH 9.55); `"retain"` leaves the ocean at 5.7e-7 molal H₂ (README §7, Gas).

## 2. Lucas's production case

k = 1e-7 m², full-core layer, 12 orbits, one orbit per step, 160 °C, 15 wt% IOM.

```{r production}
f <- ph$generate_phreeqc_input_tidal_kinetic(output_dir = "phreeqc_inputs/ex2", mode = "ungrouped",
                                             n_orbital_cycles = 12, porewater_temp = 160, substeps = 1,
                                             trace_C_molal = 1e-14)
x <- run_input(f)                     # 5-9 minutes
ocean <- x[seq(4, nrow(x), 4), ]      # MIX 2 rows: the ocean at the end of each orbit
pore  <- x[seq(1, nrow(x), 4), ]      # REACT rows: porewater, rock, pore gas
data.frame(orbit = 1:12, pH = ocean$pH, H2 = ocean$m_H2, DIC = ocean$C, bubble_L = pore$Vgas_L, Vgas_Vpore = pore$Vgas_Vpore)
bulk_density(sub("\\.pqi$", ".csv", f), porosity = sim$params$porosity)$summary[c(1, 13), ]
```

Expect at orbit 12 (the default `pore_gas_fate = "to_ocean"`; 718 s; numbers of 2026-10-31): ocean pH
10.63, H₂ 0.065 molal (saturated at 66.7 atm), DIC 3.4e-8 molal, 0.84 L of ocean gas; a pore bubble of
0.56 L after the first orbit (3.6× the pore volume) that has gone to the ocean by orbit 12 (5e-4 L);
ρ_solid 2.92 → 2.76 g/cm³. The bubble is the metal's H₂: Fe and Ni corrode completely in the first step
(D6, an accepted idealisation of early outgassing). `h2_budget()` and `scale_to_core()` give the H₂
inventory (1.5e20 mol in the ocean gas for the whole core; README §6).

## 3. A 100 °C organic vs blank pair

`pair_organic_run()` runs the case and a blank with the same mineral inventory and no organics,
and returns the organics' contribution to the ocean by difference.

```{r pair}
pr <- pair_organic_run(ph, "tidal_kinetic", mode = "ungrouped", n_orbital_cycles = 2, porewater_temp = 100,
                       trace_C_molal = 1e-14, output_dir = "phreeqc_inputs/ex3")
pr$contribution
```

Expect (5-20 minutes): after 2 orbits the organics add 6.5e-13 molal DIC to the ocean (the blank's
is the 1e-14 seed), ~2e-19 molal Mtg and NH₄⁺, and no H₂ (6e-12 molal against 2.7e-6 from the
metal, which is the same in both).

## 4. The cometary-ice ocean

An option, not the default: the ocean starts with comet 67P ice depleted as in Miller et al. (2026)
Table 5 (v = 0.02, from Titan's N budget). The ices react into the ocean before the first orbit;
`<base>_initial_ocean.csv` records the result.

```{r cometary}
f <- ph$generate_phreeqc_input_tidal_kinetic(output_dir = "phreeqc_inputs/ex4", mode = "ungrouped",
                                             n_orbital_cycles = 2, porewater_temp = 100, trace_C_molal = 1e-14,
                                             initial_ocean = cometary_ice_ocean())
x <- run_input(f)
o0 <- read.delim(list.files(dirname(f), "_initial_ocean\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE), check.names = FALSE, strip.white = TRUE)
names(o0) <- trimws(names(o0)); o0[, c("pH", "C", "Mtg", "m_SO4-2", "m_HSO4-", "m_H2S", "m_H2", "Vgas_L")]
```

Expect for the starting ocean (NH₃ included, the default since 10-31): pH 2.08, 0.0866 molal DIC (all
C(+4)), Mtg 0.0102, S(+6) 0.0094 and S(−2) 0.0028 molal, 7.4e-3 molal NH₄⁺, no bubble. With ~0.087 molal DIC from the start, the organics' carbon can only
be found by the paired difference (example 3 with `initial_ocean = cometary_ice_ocean()`).
`cometary_ice_ocean(include_O2 = FALSE)` leaves sulfide unoxidised and 0.031 molal H₂ (pH 3.8);
`include_NH3 = FALSE` gives Miller et al.'s Table 5 as printed (pH 1.85); `include_less_volatile = TRUE`
adds 21 less-volatile ices (DIC 0.56 molal, pH 5.8, an H₂ bubble; README §6); `f` scales the load.

## 5. The pore-gas bracket

The production case under both fates of the pore bubble, each with its blank.

```{r bracket}
for (fate in c("retain", "to_ocean")) {
  pr <- pair_organic_run(ph, "tidal_kinetic", mode = "ungrouped", n_orbital_cycles = 12, porewater_temp = 160,
                         substeps = 1, pore_gas_fate = fate, trace_C_molal = 1e-14,
                         output_dir = file.path("phreeqc_inputs/ex5", fate))
  print(pr$contribution)
}
```

Expect at orbit 12: ocean H₂ 1.5e-5 (retain) vs 6.5e-2 molal (to_ocean, saturated at 66.7 atm, with
0.82 L of ocean gas); the organic DIC is the same, 1.29e-7 molal; organic Mtg 1e-13 vs 1.8e-9 molal
(plus 2.4e-8 mol in the ocean gas). PROGRESS Part 7 has the full table at 150 and 160 °C.
